args.text: [lane-plover] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to an old server after a site moves, causing outages or errors. (2) Slow recovery: failover and emergency changes take effect late, because resolvers keep serving the old answer until it expires. (3) Prolonged poisoning: if a forged answer enters a cache, it stays there and misleads users for longer.

[lane-plover] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave the sender unsure whether a request worked, so retrying is often the only safe choice. If the request is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause harm such as a double payment or a duplicate order.

[lane-plover] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (a time-ordered universally unique identifier) as a primary key: (1) Good for storage: new keys sort roughly by creation time, so index inserts stay mostly at the end and avoid the scattered writes of random keys. (2) Weaker privacy: the key reveals when a row was created, and ids are easier to guess than fully random ones. Keys are also 16 bytes, larger than a typical 8-byte integer, so indexes take more space.

[lane-plover] A write-ahead log is a record of each change that a database writes to durable storage before it alters the main data files. If the system crashes part-way through, it can replay the log to restore a consistent state, so committed work is not lost and half-finished work can be undone.

[lane-plover] Pinning a client version in a benchmark matters for two reasons. (1) Fair comparison: if the client changes between runs, a difference in results may come from the client rather than the system being tested. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the test later and get comparable results, because the same code is being measured.

[lane-plover] Backpressure is a way for a queue to signal producers to slow down or pause when consumers cannot keep up. It stops the queue growing without limit, which protects memory and keeps waiting times predictable, usually by blocking, rejecting or throttling new work.

[lane-plover] A cron job can run twice when (1) two servers carry the same schedule, or (2) a slow run is still going when the next one starts. One guard is a lock, such as a lock file or database lock, that makes a second copy exit straight away.

[lane-plover] A tombstone is a marker saved in place of a deleted item in a replicated store. It lets every copy learn about the deletion, so an out-of-date copy cannot bring the item back; the marker is removed only after a safe waiting period.

[lane-plover] Two signs a test is flaky rather than failing: (1) it passes and fails on the same code with no change between runs; (2) it fails only sometimes, for example under heavy load, in a certain order, or at certain times, and a plain re-run often passes.

[lane-plover] A lease is a lock that expires after a set time. If one machine's clock runs fast or slow compared with another's, it may think its lease is still valid after the lock service has given it to someone else. Then two holders act at once, so the lock no longer protects the shared work.
